chunks.title: Business visa
chunks.content:
Uzbekistan Business Visa

Summary

The Uzbekistan Business Visa is designed for foreign nationals visiting the country for commercial purposes, meetings, and business negotiations. It is split into two primary types: the standard Business Visa (B-1/B-2) requiring a local corporate sponsor, and the Investment Visa (V-2) for significant financial contributors. Standard processing takes 2 to 10 working days through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MVD/MFA) networks or the electronic visa portal.

Overview

A business visa allows foreign professionals to enter Uzbekistan to establish corporate networks, sign contracts, or oversee existing investments. It is strictly non-employment; individuals looking to earn a local salary must secure a separate work permit and work visa (E-type).

Eligibility

The business visa categories are available to:

Corporate Executives & Managers: Individuals representing foreign companies for market research or partnership setups.

Investors: High-net-worth individuals purchasing shares, setting up local entities, or funding infrastructure.

Technical Specialists: Consultants visiting local branches for short-term corporate oversight or machinery setups.

Requirements

To qualify for a business visa, an applicant must:

Be invited by a legally registered legal entity (company) within Uzbekistan.

Secure an official Letter of Invitation (LOI) approved by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (except for nationalities eligible for simplified procedures).

Possess a passport valid for at least 3 months beyond the intended visa expiration date.

Required Documents

The application package differs based on the sub-category, but generally requires:

Visa Application Form: Completed online or in print with a passport-sized photo.

chunks.title: Business visa
chunks.content:
Visa Application Form: Completed online or in print with a passport-sized photo.

Valid Passport: Clear copy of the biometric data page.

Letter of Invitation (LOI): Issued by the inviting company in Uzbekistan and stamped by the MFA.

Corporate Charter / License: A copy of the inviting company's state registration documents.

Employment Proof: A formal letter from the applicant’s foreign employer stating their corporate position and purpose of travel.

Investment Proof (For V-2 Track): Bank certificates or corporate certificates showing a minimum investment or share purchase of at least $10,000 to $300,000 depending on the target framework.

Application Steps

Sponsor Request: The inviting company in Uzbekistan submits a request to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the dedicated corporate portal to generate the LOI telex.

LOI Issuance: The MFA reviews the company's standing and issues a unique confirmation/telex code.

Application Submission:

Option A (Embassy): The applicant submits the paperwork and the telex code to the nearest Uzbek Consulate.

Option B (E-Visa): For specific business categories, the applicant applies directly via the e-visa.gov.uz portal using the corporate invite details.

Interview and Collection: Collect the physical sticker visa at the consulate or download the electronic PDF voucher.

Processing Time

LOI Approval (MFA): Takes 5 to 10 working days.

Consular/E-Visa Processing: Takes 2 to 5 working days once the LOI code is issued.

Fees

Standard E-Visa (Single-entry Business): Consular fees average $20 to $30.

Multiple-Entry Business Visa (Consulate-issued): Fees range from $150 to $350 depending on the visa duration (up to 1 year) and the applicant's citizenship due to bilateral reciprocity agreements.

Validity

chunks.title: Business visa
chunks.content:
Validity

Single or Double-Entry: Typically valid for 30 days to 90 days.

Multiple-Entry (B-2): Valid for 6 months or 1 year, allowing multiple entries with a cap on continuous days spent per visit (usually 90 days per entry).

Investment Visa (V-2): Valid for up to 3 years with unrestricted multi-entry rights.

Renewal

In-Country Extensions: Business visas can rarely be extended inside the country unless there is an emergency or an explicit request submitted by an inviting Ministry or large state enterprise to the Migration and Citizenship Department.

Visa Run: Applicants typically need to exit Uzbekistan and apply for a new business telex/visa from abroad.

Restrictions

No Local Salary: You cannot be directly employed or receive a salary from an Uzbek entity under a business visa.

Strict Company Affiliation: You must only engage in business operations connected to the specific local company that sponsored your original LOI.

Registration Mandatory: Holding a business visa does not bypass the requirement to register your temporary address within 3 working days of arrival.

Exceptions

Visa-Free Nationalities: Citizens of certain countries (e.g., EU nationals, Turkey, UAE) can enter Uzbekistan visa-free for 30 days or 90 days and can conduct basic business meetings without a formal business visa.

IT Park Residents: Foreign investors or specialists affiliated with the Uzbekistan IT Park enjoy expedited visa processes and direct exemptions from standard local labor market testing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I switch from an E-visa to a long-term business visa inside Uzbekistan? No. Changing your visa category inside the country is generally prohibited. You must leave and re-enter with the appropriate consular-issued business sticker.

chunks.title: Business visa
chunks.content:
Can I switch from an E-visa to a long-term business visa inside Uzbekistan? No. Changing your visa category inside the country is generally prohibited. You must leave and re-enter with the appropriate consular-issued business sticker.

Can I open a local bank account with a business visa? Yes. You can open an Uzbek bank account using your passport, business visa, temporary registration slip, and a local PINFL number.

Does a business visa guarantee entry? No. Border control officials hold final authorization rights and can request proof of accommodation, return tickets, or your company's physical contact info at the gate.

Official Sources & Related Documents

Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Uzbekistan (mfa.uz): The regulatory authority for all LOI validations and consular sticker issuances.

Official E-Visa Portal (e-visa.gov.uz): The formal portal used for short-term commercial and electronic entry applications.

Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 408: Governs the entry, exit, and temporary residence rules for foreign professionals and commercial operators.

chunks.title: Electronic visa
chunks.content:
An e-Visa to Uzbekistan can be obtained completely online through the official government portal e-visa.gov.uz. This system completely eliminates the need to visit an embassy or consular office. [1, 2, 3]

Cost and Visa Types

The processing fee varies depending on the number of entries you require, and payments can be made online via an international credit or debit card (such as Visa): [3, 4]

Single-Entry: 20 USD

Double-Entry: 35 USD

Multiple-Entry: 50 USD [5]

Validity and Stay Duration

Duration of Stay: You are allowed to stay in Uzbekistan for up to 30 days per visit.

Validity Window: The e-Visa remains valid for 90 days from the exact date it is issued. You can enter the country at any point during this 90-day window. [6, 7, 8, 9]

Processing Time

You must apply at least 3 working days before your planned trip.

Applications are typically processed within 2 working days (excluding the day of filing). Once approved, the electronic visa is sent directly to your email in PDF format. [6, 8, 10]

Document Requirements

When filling out the online application form, you will need to upload digital copies of the following: [2, 3]

Passport Data Page: A clear, readable scan of your passport's main page (the passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure date).

Passport Photo: A digital, passport-style photograph (35x45 mm size, white background, under 1 MB file size). [2, 4]

Who Needs an e-Visa?

Citizens of countries that do not have bilateral visa-free entry agreements with Uzbekistan must apply for an e-Visa. This primarily includes citizens of: [11]

Albania Algeria Angola Bhutan Bolivia Cabo Verde Cambodia Cameroon Colombia Côte d’Ivoire Ecuador Egypt Fiji Gabon Ghana Guyana

chunks.title: Electronic visa
chunks.content:
Albania Algeria Angola Bhutan Bolivia Cabo Verde Cambodia Cameroon Colombia Côte d’Ivoire Ecuador Egypt Fiji Gabon Ghana Guyana

To apply for an Uzbekistan electronic visa, you must submit your application through the official government portal at e-visa.gov.uz. Avoid third-party websites that charge extra processing fees. [1, 2]

Below is the complete step-by-step application guideline based on the official requirements for 2026.

Overview of Visa Types and Fees

Consular fees depend entirely on the number of entries you require. The fee is non-refundable, even if your application is denied. [3]

Note: Your 90-day validity window begins the moment your application is processed, not on your day of arrival. You can enter Uzbekistan at any point within this 90-day window. [4]

Required Documents & Photo Specifications

Before opening the application portal, prepare the following digital assets according to strict Uzbek technical guidelines:

Passport Scan:

Must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure date (some borders recommend 6 months).

Upload only the main bio-data page.

File size must not exceed 500 KB and the text must be easily readable. [2, 5, 6, 7]

Digital Passport Photo:

Dimensions must be exactly 35x40 mm.

Resolution must be 300 dpi.

File size must be under 1 MB.

Must feature a plain white background with a clear frontal view of your face. [2, 5]

Accommodation Info: The name and physical address of your first hotel or accommodation. [2]

chunks.title: Electronic visa
chunks.content:
Accommodation Info: The name and physical address of your first hotel or accommodation. [2]

Step-by-Step Application Process

Select Preliminary Information: Go to the official website and input your nationality, travel document type, and your purpose of visit (Tourist). [8, 9]

Define Travel Dates: Input your intended date of entry into the country. [10]

Enter Personal Data: Input your biographical details exactly as they appear on your passport. Mistakes here will lead to entry denial at the border. [1, 2, 8]

Upload Documents: Attach your pre-formatted passport scan and digital photo. [1, 5]

Email Activation: Enter a valid, active email address. The system will send you an automated message containing an activation code/link. You must enter this code on the portal to verify your account. [1, 2, 10]

Pay the Consular Fee: Complete the online payment using an international Visa or payment card. The card does not need to be under your name. [3, 9, 11]

Processing Time and Status Check

Timeline: The standard turnaround is 3 working days (excluding the day you submitted the application). Always apply at least 3 business days before flying. [3, 11, 12]

Tracking: You can monitor your application's progress directly on the e-visa.gov.uz/status page by inputting your unique activation code. [10]

Delivery: Once approved, a PDF version of the e-visa is sent to your email. Print a physical copy of this PDF; border control requires you to keep it alongside your passport during your stay. [1, 9, 11]

chunks.title: Family reunification and private visits
chunks.content:
Family reunification

Uzbekistan issues Family Visas (Category "O-2") to foreign nationals seeking long-term stay for family reunification with relatives who are citizens of Uzbekistan. The process requires an official invitation sponsored by the inviting relative through the territorial migration authorities of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

Summary

Visa Type: Family Guest Visa (Category O-2).

Validity: Issued for up to 1 year with multiple entry options, depending on the track.

Key Obligation: Mandatory local residence registration within 3 working days of arrival.

Overview

Family reunification in Uzbekistan is primarily managed through the "O-2" visa framework, designed for close relatives of Uzbek citizens. It serves as a stepping stone for foreigners who wish to live long-term with their families in Uzbekistan. An active O-2 visa allows the holder to remain in the country legally without needing tourist or business visa renewals, though it does not automatically grant permanent residency.

Eligibility

The following close relatives of citizens of the Republic of Uzbekistan are eligible to apply for family reunification under the O-2 track:

Spouses: Legally married husbands or wives.

Children: Biological or legally adopted children.

Parents: Parents or legal guardians of Uzbek citizens.

Siblings: Biological brothers and sisters (under specific dependency or hosting criteria).

Requirements

Official Invitation: The inviting relative in Uzbekistan must file an official invitation request through their local migration office.

Proof of Kinship: Legal and apostilled/legalized documents proving the exact family relationship are strictly required.

chunks.title: Family reunification and private visits
chunks.content:
Proof of Kinship: Legal and apostilled/legalized documents proving the exact family relationship are strictly required.

Financial & Housing Support: The inviting host must guarantee that they have the means and space to accommodate the foreign relative.

Required Documents

The standard application dossier required to initiate the family visa track includes:

Application Steps

Local Filing: The inviting relative visits their local territorial Migration and Citizenship Department (formerly OVIR) in Uzbekistan to submit the invitation request.

Security Clearance: Migration authorities review the host's documents and issue an approved invitation code/telex.

Visa Application: The foreign relative takes this approval code to the nearest Uzbek Embassy/Consulate or applies via the https://visa.mfa.uz/ if eligible.

Entry & Registration: Upon arrival in Uzbekistan, the foreigner must register their physical address via the hotel or the host's Emehmon Portal within 3 working days.

PR Application (Optional): If the applicant qualifies for Permanent Residence (e.g., through marriage or direct descent), they can transition to apply for a Permanent Residence Permit (Vid na Zhitelstvo) at the migration office.

Processing Time

Invitation Clearance in Uzbekistan: 14 to 30 days for background checks and processing.

Consular Visa Issuance: 3 to 7 working days once the embassy receives the migration department's clearance.

Fees

Local Invitation Fee: A minor administrative state duty (calculated based on the current Base Calculation Amount).

Consular Visa Fee: Ranges from $40 to $160 depending on the duration (single vs. multiple entry) and the applicant's nationality.

Validity

Initial Visa: Typically issued for 3 to 12 months as a multiple-entry visa.

chunks.title: Family reunification and private visits
chunks.content:
Initial Visa: Typically issued for 3 to 12 months as a multiple-entry visa.

Permanent Transition: If a Permanent Residence Permit is successfully granted later, the physical permit card is issued for 5 years (or up to the validity of the foreign passport).

Renewal

Timeline: O-2 visa extensions must be requested at local migration offices at least 10-15 working days before expiration.

Basis: Continued validity of the family relationship (e.g., active marriage) and sustained local residence registration.

Restrictions

No Direct Work Rights: Holding an O-2 family visa does not grant immediate commercial employment rights. The foreigner must still obtain a standard work permit from the Agency for External Labor Migration to work legally.

Address Locking: The foreigner must physically reside at the address where they are registered. Moving or staying elsewhere without updating the migration file triggers administrative fines.

Exceptions

CIS Visa-Free Countries: Relatives holding passports from visa-free nations (like Russia, Kazakhstan, or Belarus) do not need an O-2 visa. They enter visa-free and can apply directly for long-term temporary registration or transition directly to permanent residency processing based on family ties.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does marrying an Uzbek citizen give me immediate citizenship? No. Marriage grants eligibility for a Permanent Residence Permit first. Under current laws, citizenship via marriage requires a period of permanent residency and meeting specific integration and legal criteria.

chunks.title: Family reunification and private visits
chunks.content:
Does marrying an Uzbek citizen give me immediate citizenship? No. Marriage grants eligibility for a Permanent Residence Permit first. Under current laws, citizenship via marriage requires a period of permanent residency and meeting specific integration and legal criteria.

Can I apply for family reunification entirely online? The initial invitation must be verified and processed through the physical migration department in Uzbekistan by your relative. However, once approved, the actual visa application can often be finalized via the digital consular networks.

Official Sources

Consular Track Information: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) of Uzbekistan

Housing Registrations: E-mehmon Digital Portal

Related Documents

Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens and Stateless Persons."

Family Code of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

Category | Required Documents

Identity | National passport of the applicant and the internal passport/ID-card of the inviting Uzbek citizen.

Kinship Proof | Marriage certificate, birth certificates, or adoption papers (translated and notarized).

Host Guarantee | Notarized consent form from the property owner agreeing to host the foreign relative.

Application | Completed visa application form from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA).

Income Proof | Financial statements or employment proof from the inviting relative (if requested by local migration desks).

chunks.title: Overstay penalties and exit
chunks.content:
Overstay penalties

Overstaying a visa or failing to fulfill registration requirements in Uzbekistan results in tiered monetary fines based on the duration of the violation, potential deportation, and entry bans. Under Article 225 of the Administrative Responsibility Code, penalties are calculated using the country's Base Calculation Amount (BCA/BHM). [1, 2]

Tiered Fine Structure

Fines do not accrue strictly day-by-day but are categorized by duration blocks: [1]

Up to 10 Days: A fine of 5 BCA.

11 to 30 Days: A fine of 10 BCA.

More than 30 Days: A fine of 20 BCA. [1]

(Note: Minor travelers under the age of 18 are legally exempt from administrative fines for overstaying or violating residency regulations). [2]

Escalated Penalties & Sanctions

Failing to settle the fine immediately or repeating the violation introduces severe legal mechanisms:

Deportation & 1-Year Ban: If you are unable or refuse to pay the administrative overstay fine, you will be formally expelled from the country and issued a 1-year entry ban. [2]

3-Year Ban: Committing a repeated overstay or registration violation within a single calendar year triggers immediate deportation and a 3-year entry ban. [2, 3]

Host Liability: Local residents or businesses who host a foreigner but fail to register them properly or help them leave upon visa expiration face independent, separate fines. [4]

Critical Next Steps if You Overstay

If you realize you have overstayed your visa or missed the 3-day registration window, do not wait until your departure day at the airport gates:

Visit Migration Offices: Report immediately to the local territorial Migration and Citizenship Assessment Department (formerly known as OVIR). [5]

chunks.title: Overstay penalties and exit
chunks.content:
Visit Migration Offices: Report immediately to the local territorial Migration and Citizenship Assessment Department (formerly known as OVIR). [5]

Obtain an Exit Visa: You must officially clear the fine at a bank desk and obtain a temporary documentation extension or explicit exit visa clearance prior to boarding a departing flight.

If you are currently facing an overstay, tell me how many days you have overstayed and your current location in Uzbekistan. I can provide details on the nearest migration office.

chunks.title: Passport validity requirements
chunks.content:
To obtain a visa and enter Uzbekistan, your passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond the expiration date of your visa or your intended period of stay. [1, 2]

However, many international airlines and border control authorities strongly recommend having 6 months of passport validity from your date of entry to prevent any boarding or transit complications. [2, 3]

📑 Complete Passport Criteria for Uzbekistan

Validity Duration: 3 months minimum past your stay/visa expiration (6 months recommended). [1, 2]

Blank Pages: Your passport must contain at least 1 to 2 completely blank visa pages for entry and exit border stamps. [4, 5]

Physical Condition: The passport must be in good condition, completely intact, and free of any tears, water damage, or unofficial markings. [6]

Matching Information: The passport you use to cross the border must exactly match the passport details provided during your E-visa application. If you renew your passport after receiving an E-visa, the visa becomes invalid and you must reapply with your new passport. [2, 7]

chunks.title: Permanent residence in Uzbekistan
chunks.content:
Here is the complete, comprehensive guide to obtaining and maintaining Permanent Residence (PR) in Uzbekistan based on current immigration frameworks and updated legislation.

Summary

Foreign nationals can secure permanent residence in Uzbekistan via three primary tracks: real estate investments starting at $100,000 to $300,000, family reunification, or employment status as a highly qualified specialist. The review process takes up to 1 to 2 months (68 working days). The card grants the right to legally reside, work, and study in the country, is issued for a 5-year renewable term, and carries zero physical presence requirements for tax residency under specific elite economic structures.

Overview

A permanent residence permit (Вид на жительство) serves as an official identification document for foreign citizens and stateless persons living in Uzbekistan. Holding PR permits long-term settlement, employment without a standalone work permit, and streamlined access to state healthcare and education networks.

Eligibility

The right to apply for a permanent residence permit is granted to the following groups:

Property Investors: Foreigners purchasing newly constructed primary residential real estate.

Family Members: Spouses, children, or dependent parents of citizens of Uzbekistan or existing PR holders.

Highly Qualified Specialists: Internationally recognized professionals or scientists invited to work in Uzbekistan.

Former Citizens & Stateless Persons: Individuals born in the territory or those with deep historical ties.

Requirements

To meet basic regulatory criteria, an applicant must:

Have a clean criminal record.

Pose no threat to national security or public health.

chunks.title: Permanent residence in Uzbekistan
chunks.content:
Pose no threat to national security or public health.

Obtain a PINFL (Personal Identification Number of an Individual) via a Public Services Center.

Possess a legal residential address where the property owner provides documented consent.

Required Documents

Applicants must submit a complete application package including:

Application form: Two completed copies in Uzbek or Russian.

Valid Foreign Passport: Must have at least 6 months of validity remaining.

Notarized Translations: Passport and external documents translated into Uzbek.

Police Clearance Certificate: Background check from the country of origin.

Medical Clearances: Comprehensive health check including a mandatory HIV-negative certificate from an authorized state clinic.

Proof of Housing: Cadastral ownership documents or a notarized host's letter of consent to register the applicant.

Financial Proof: Bank statements proving economic self-sufficiency.

Passport Photos: Four copies (3.5 x 4.5 cm) on a white background.

Track-Specific Documents: Marriage/birth certificates for family tracks, or bank certificates showing the nominal value of capital/shares for business paths.

Application Steps

Legal Entry & Immediate Registration: Enter Uzbekistan on a valid visa or visa-free entry. Register your temporary stay address at the local migration office or through the "E-guest" program within 3 working days.

Obtain PINFL: Visit a Public Services Center to generate your identity number.

Medical Checks: Visit an authorized domestic clinic for the required laboratory tests.

Notarization: Gather, translate, and notarize your foreign background papers and certificates.

chunks.title: Permanent residence in Uzbekistan
chunks.content:
Notarization: Gather, translate, and notarize your foreign background papers and certificates.

Submission: Apply in person through the Migration and Citizenship Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MVD), a Public Services Center, or digitally via the EPIGU (My.gov.uz) online portal. Both the applicant and property owner must confirm consent, using Face-ID or Mobile-ID if submitted online.

Processing Time

Standard Route: Up to 1 month for review by the regional competent authorities.

Investment Route: Up to 68 working days for finalized processing and distribution of the physical permit card.

Fees

Document Review & Registration: Paid at a standard rate of 20% of the minimum wage (BHM/BRV).

Gold Visa Multi-Year Pass Option: A fast-track 5-year permit can be explicitly obtained via an up-front statutory processing fee of $200,000 for the primary applicant and $100,000 per family member.

Validity & Renewal

Standard Terms: The residence permit is issued for a duration of 5 years. It cannot exceed the remaining validity of the holder's national passport.

Senior Categories: For individuals who have reached 60 years of age, the permit is issued for 10 years or for the remainder of their passport validity. For stateless seniors, it is permanent.

Renewal: Applications for extension can be renewed up to 5 times before requiring a new physical booklet update.

Restrictions

Land Ownership: Foreign residents can own buildings and infrastructure but are forbidden from directly owning agricultural or residential land. Land use is restricted to long-term leases (up to 49 years).

Political Rights: PR holders do not possess voting rights and cannot hold public office.

chunks.title: Permanent residence in Uzbekistan
chunks.content:
Political Rights: PR holders do not possess voting rights and cannot hold public office.

Dual Citizenship: Uzbekistan strictly forbids dual nationality. PR does not grant an additional passport, and moving from PR to naturalized citizenship requires the formal renunciation of your original citizenship.

Exceptions

Special Tax Regime: Under updated financial incentives, high-net-worth individuals and corporate board executives can achieve formal tax residency with only 30 days of physical presence within a 12-month period, circumventing the standard 183-day rule.

Fee Exemptions: Individuals fully supported or secured by the state are exempt from paying government duties on the issuance or extension of residence documents.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a standard work visa automatically convert into permanent residence? No. Standard employment time or tax tracking does not guarantee PR. An applicant must still independently qualify through investment, direct family roots, or elite talent categories.

What happens if my PR application is refused? If refused, you must leave the region within 3 days of receiving notice. However, you may stay temporarily under standard tourist or commercial visas if you own legally acquired property, hold valid local employment, or are undergoing hospital treatment.

Can I qualify for PR by buying a secondary-market apartment? No. The investment pathway strictly requires purchasing newly built property on the primary real estate market.

Official Sources & Related Documents

chunks.title: Registration of foreigners
chunks.content:
Registration of foreigners

Summary

All foreign nationals visiting Uzbekistan must register their place of stay within 3 working days of arrival. Registration is handled automatically by hotels or licensed guest houses. If staying in private accommodations (e.g., Airbnb, friends), registration must be completed online via the E-mehmon system or via EPIGU, requiring biometric verification (Face-ID/Mobile-ID) from both the visitor and the property owner. Failing to register results in heavy administrative fines. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Overview

Temporary registration (Vaqtincha roʻyxatdan oʻtish) tracks the temporary location of foreign citizens and stateless persons for tourism, business, or personal visits. Under recent legislative updates, the regulatory focus has shifted to the hosting party (landlords and hotels), holding them legally responsible for submitting guest information. [4, 6, 7]

Eligibility

Registration applies to:

All foreign tourists staying in hotels, hostels, resorts, or campsites.

Private guests staying with relatives, friends, or in rented apartments.

Foreign employees, students, and medical patients residing in the country temporarily. [3, 8, 9, 10]

Requirements

To successfully register your stay, you must:

Apply within 3 business days following the day of your entry.

Stay only at the exact physical address provided during registration.

Coordinate directly with your property owner, who must log into the portal using their OneID/MyID account. [2, 5, 7, 10, 11]

Required Documents

If your host registers you or you register a private stay, you will need:

Valid International Passport: Showing your full biometrics and biometric page.

Entry Border Stamp: Proof of the entry date and border checkpoint location.

chunks.title: Registration of foreigners
chunks.content:
Entry Border Stamp: Proof of the entry date and border checkpoint location.

Cadastral Number: The legal property identifier number of the host's apartment or house.

PINFL: Needed primarily for long-term stays or extensions exceeding 30 days. [1, 7, 11, 12]

Application Steps

For Hotel/Hostel Bookings:

Check-In: Hand your passport to the front desk at check-in.

Automatic Upload: The staff enters your details into the commercial E-mehmon portal.

Receipt Collection: Request your paper registration slip (with a QR code) before checking out. [4, 6, 9]

For Private/Rented Housing:

Access Portal: The landlord logs into emehmon.uz or my.gov.uz.

Enter Data: The landlord fills out the "Arrival Guest List" with your passport and entry details.

Biometric Consent: Under Resolution No. 224, both parties verify their identification using Face-ID or Mobile-ID via the app.

Download Voucher: Save and print the generated electronic registration form. [5, 6, 11]

Processing Time

Instantaneous: Electronic submission through the E-mehmon application issues the registration slip immediately upon data submission and fee settlement. [6]

Fees

Hotels/Hostels: The mandatory tourist tax (ranging roughly from $2 to $5 per night depending on accommodation tier) is usually integrated directly into your room rate or invoiced at checkout.

Private Residences: If staying with family or friends for non-commercial purposes, a lower flat processing fee is calculated via the online portal system. [10, 11]

Validity

Short-Term Tourist Registration: Valid for the exact duration of your paid booking or declared itinerary up to 30 days.

chunks.title: Registration of foreigners
chunks.content:
Short-Term Tourist Registration: Valid for the exact duration of your paid booking or declared itinerary up to 30 days.

Long-Term Temporary Registration: Can be granted for up to 6 months to 1 year for foreigners holding valid work permits, student enrollments, or multi-entry business visas. [10, 12]

Renewal

Changing Accommodations: If you move to a new city or another hotel, the new provider must register your presence fresh within 3 days.

Extensions: Long-term extensions require an application submitted by your inviting company, school, or relative to the local Migration and Citizenship Department (Passport Office / OVIR) before your current permit expires. [9, 13]

Restrictions

No Unauthorized Movement: You cannot legally live at an address different from the registered text location on your e-registration form.

Strict Timelines: Weekends and national holidays do not pause the 3-day clock; applications must be initiated promptly.

Work Prohibition: Tourist registration does not grant the right to engage in local commercial activities or employment. [7, 10, 12]

Exceptions

The following categories are exempt from standard temporary registration requirements: [13]

Foreigners staying in the country for fewer than 3 working days.

Children under 16 years of age.

Heads of foreign states, government delegations, and individuals traveling on UN passports.

Diplomatic staff and individuals accredited by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA). [2, 10, 13]

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to keep the physical paper registration slips? Yes. Keep all paper slips or digital QR vouchers until you exit the country. Border control officers occasionally check them at airport immigration.

chunks.title: Registration of foreigners
chunks.content:
Do I need to keep the physical paper registration slips? Yes. Keep all paper slips or digital QR vouchers until you exit the country. Border control officers occasionally check them at airport immigration.

What happens if my landlord refuses to register me? You are in legal jeopardy. You must change accommodations to a hotel or an authorized host who will log into E-mehmon immediately to avoid systemic fines.

Can I register myself if I am wild camping or overlanding? Yes. Independent tourists staying in tents or camper vans can log directly into E-mehmon, select the independent traveler track, and pay the corresponding tourist fees via bank card. [6, 13]

Official Sources & Related Documents

Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (my.gov.uz): For processing residential stays, Face-ID tracking, and long-term registrations.

Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 224: Establishes modern biometric authorization frameworks and dual-party consent rules.

Law No. LRU-1074: Specifies the legal obligations of local property owners and housing managers to register foreign guests. [3, 4, 5, 12, 14]

chunks.title: Student visas
chunks.content:
Student visas

Uzbekistan issues Student Visas (Category "A-2") to foreign nationals who are officially enrolled in licensed higher or secondary specialized educational institutions across the country. The process requires an official invitation sponsored by the host educational institution through the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Innovations.

Summary

Visa Type: Student Visa (Category A-2).

Validity: Issued for the duration of the academic period (typically up to 1 year, renewable).

Key Obligation: Mandatory local residence registration within 3 working days of arrival.

Overview

The student visa in Uzbekistan is designed for long-term academic stays. It cannot be issued automatically upon purchasing short-term private courses; it requires a strict institutional linkage between the student, the university, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA). An active A-2 visa functions as a multiple-entry pass throughout its duration.

Eligibility

The following foreign nationals are eligible to apply for an A-2 student visa:

Individuals who have passed the entrance exams or admission interviews at a licensed Uzbek university.

Students enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's, Ph.D. programs, or long-term clinical/academic internships.

International students arriving under formal academic exchange or bilateral university mobility agreements.

Requirements

Official Visa Support (Telex): The primary legal basis for the visa is an invitation code approved by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the university’s request.

Full-Time/On-Campus Enrollment: Distance learning or part-time/correspondence formats do not generally qualify a student for a long-term residence track.

chunks.title: Student visas
chunks.content:
Full-Time/On-Campus Enrollment: Distance learning or part-time/correspondence formats do not generally qualify a student for a long-term residence track.

Financial Solvency: Proof of capability to cover tuition fees, housing, and general cost of living.

Required Documents

The standard application dossier required at the consulate or online visa portal includes:

Application Steps

Admission: Finalize your enrollment contract with the Uzbek university and pay the initial tuition fee installment.

Telex Request: The international department of the university submits your dossier to the MFA to request formal visa support.

Obtain Code: The university provides you with the completed MFA confirmation number (Telex number).

Visa Submission: Submit your application to the nearest Embassy/Consulate of Uzbekistan or via the https://visa.mfa.uz/ if applicable to your nationality.

Arrival & Registration: Upon crossing the border, ensure the university helps you secure your temporary residence registration within 3 working days.

Processing Time

MFA Visa Support (Telex Approval): 14 to 30 days depending on institutional queues.

Consular Processing: 3 to 7 working days once the Telex code has been officially received.

Fees

Consular Fee: Ranges from $40 to $200 depending on the applicant's nationality and the requested entry frequency (single vs. multiple entry).

Administrative Fees: Some universities may charge separate internal processing fees for document handling.

Validity

Initial Entry: Usually granted for 1 to 3 months to allow the student to travel and enter the country.

In-Country Extension: Once you clear registration with your university, it is extended up to 1 year (covering the current academic year block).

Renewal

chunks.title: Student visas
chunks.content:
Renewal

Timeline: Applications for renewal must be submitted to the local Migration Department (UvaOG) at least 15–20 days prior to the expiry of the current visa.

Basis: A new rectoral decree confirming your advancement to the next academic semester and verification of up-to-date tuition payments.

Restrictions

No Direct Employment: The A-2 student visa does not grant full commercial work rights. Foreign students cannot work legally unless they acquire a separate work permit from the Agency for External Labor Migration.

Institutional Lock: Your visa is legally tied to your specific university. If you drop out, are expelled, or transfer, your visa is immediately canceled, and you must exit the country to re-apply.

Exceptions

CIS Country Nationals: Students holding passports from visa-free CIS nations (e.g., Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Tajikistan) do not need an A-2 student visa. They study purely based on their national passport and a renewable temporary registration certificate.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I enter Uzbekistan on a tourist visa and change it to a student visa inside the country? No. Officially switching visa categories from a tourist track to a student track without exiting the country is prohibited. You must leave Uzbekistan and return on an official student invitation track.

Where am I allowed to live during my studies? You may reside in a university dormitory or rent a private apartment. In both scenarios, either the university administration or your landlord must register your physical location on the E-mehmon system for the duration of your visa.

Official Sources

Visa Support Approvals: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) of Uzbekistan

Electronic Visa Processing: Official E-Visa Portal

Related Documents

chunks.content:
Related Documents

Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan "On the Legal Status of Foreign Citizens and Stateless Persons."

Cabinet of Ministers Resolution on the Rules of Entry, Exit, and Residence for Foreign Nationals.

Category | Required Documents

Identity | National passport valid for at least 6 months past the requested visa expiry date.

Authorization | Official letter or approved Telex invitation code from the MFA of Uzbekistan.

Application | Completed and signed visa application form with a 3x4 cm passport photo.

Academic Proof | Official university enrollment decree or letter of acceptance from the rector.

Medical | HIV clearance certificate (mandatory for long-term residency tracks).

chunks.title: Temporary residence permits
chunks.content:
Temporary residence permits

Uzbekistan issues temporary residence permits (known as temporary registration or Vremennaya Registratsiya) to foreign nationals for durations ranging from 3 days up to 6 months per stay. The process requires active cooperation between the visitor and the host (e.g., employer, educational institution, or property owner), with modern biometric verifications like Face-ID now required for residential rentals.

Summary

Rule: Foreigners staying outside hotels must secure a temporary stay registration.

Deadline: Must be requested within 3 working days of crossing the border.

How: Processed online via state portals or in person at migration offices.

Overview

A temporary residence permit is a mandatory legal record of a foreigner's geographic stay in Uzbekistan. Unlike a Permanent Residence Permit (which takes months to issue and permits long-term settlement), the temporary version functions as a flexible stay clearance tied to a specific purpose, such as work, study, or family visits.

Eligibility

Any foreign national who has entered Uzbekistan legally (via a visa or visa-free framework) qualifies for temporary residence, provided they belong to one of these groups:

Workers: Foreigners employed by a registered Uzbek company.

Students: Individuals enrolled in licensed domestic universities.

Guests: People visiting friends or family members who own residential property.

Patients: Foreign nationals receiving long-term treatment at a local medical facility.

Requirements

Owner Consent: The landlord or host must formally approve the registration.

PINFL Requirement: Registered foreigners are assigned a Personal Identification Number (PINFL) by migration authorities.

chunks.title: Temporary residence permits
chunks.content:
PINFL Requirement: Registered foreigners are assigned a Personal Identification Number (PINFL) by migration authorities.

Geographic Boundary: You must legally live at the exact address stated on your digital registration form.

Required Documents

The required dossier varies based on the duration of your stay:

Application Steps

Legal Entry: Cross into Uzbekistan and clear border checkpoints.

Identity Setup: Apply for your PINFL number at a local Public Service Center if stay exceeds basic limits.

Owner Verification: If renting, the property owner verifies their identity using Face-ID or Mobile-ID through state portals.

Dossier Submission: Submit paperwork online via the EPIGU (My.gov.uz) Portal or in person at the Migration Department of Internal Affairs (MvaFRB).

Collection: Receive your paper or digital temporary registration certificate embedded with a protective bar-code.

Processing Time

Online Submissions: 1 working day once the landlord approves the system request.

In-Person Visits: Usually processed same-day at local migration desks.

Fees

Hotel Stays: Included directly in your nightly room rate via automated systems.

Private Stays: A state duty ranging between $10 and $20 depending on the duration and type of visa.

Validity

Range: Granted for durations from 3 days up to a maximum of 6 months.

Rule: Your residency window cannot exceed the validity period of your entry visa.

Renewal

Timeline: You must file for an extension at least 3 working days prior to your current permit expiring.

Basis: Extended upon receiving an official renewal request letter from your university, employer, or host.

Restrictions

The 3-Day Relocation Rule: If you move to a different region within Uzbekistan, you must register at your new location within 3 days.

chunks.title: Temporary residence permits
chunks.content:
The 3-Day Relocation Rule: If you move to a different region within Uzbekistan, you must register at your new location within 3 days.

Physical Address Matching: Law enforcement conducts random checks. Living at an address different from your registration triggers immediate penalizations.

Leaving the Country: Crossing an international border cancels your temporary stay file. You must re-register from scratch when you return.

Exceptions

The following groups are exempt from temporary residence registration:

Heads of foreign states, government leaders, and official state delegations.

Foreigners visiting on holiday for under 3 working days.

Crew members of international commercial aircraft, trains, or transiting vehicles.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does my hotel registration cover my whole trip? Only for the days you are checked in. If you leave the hotel to camp or sleep at a friend's house, a separate registration must be created on E-mehmon within 3 days.

Can I buy real estate to get temporary residence? Buying property unlocks Permanent Residence rather than temporary stay. The investment benchmarks are $300,000 in Tashkent or $100,000–$200,000 in other regions.

Official Sources

Digital Self-Registration: E-mehmon Tourism Portal

E-Government Interactive Submissions: Official EPIGU Portal

Related Documents

Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 224 (Regulating local residency rules)

Law on the Registration of Foreign Citizens and Stateless Persons

Document Category | Short Stay (Up to 30 Days) | Long Stay (30 Days to 6 Months)

Identity | National passport copy | Original national passport

Application | Digital form via E-mehmon | Written application & official host request letter

chunks.title: Temporary residence permits
chunks.content:
Application | Digital form via E-mehmon | Written application & official host request letter

Housing Proof | Property title deeds & owner consent | Notarized lease agreement or property deeds

Biometrics | Digital photo upload | Face-ID / Mobile-ID owner confirmation

Fees | Hotel/Tourist tax receipt | State duty payment receipt

chunks.title: Visa categories
chunks.content:
Uzbekistan issues entry visas categorized strictly by the primary purpose of your stay, which can be acquired via the E-visa portal (for select tourist/business entries) or through an embassy/consular mission (for specialized and long-term stays). [1, 2]

Over 90 nationalities (including all EU states, the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and GCC nations) enjoy visa-free entry for short stays up to 30 days. If you require a formal visa, the primary statutory categories are structured below: [3, 4, 5, 6]

Short-Term & General Travel Visas

Tourist Visa (T): Issued to leisure travelers. It can be requested as a single, double, or multiple-entry electronic visa via the official E-visa platform for stays up to 30 days. [1, 7, 8]

Business Visa (B-2): For corporate representatives visiting for meetings, contract negotiations, or trade fairs. Short-term business visits can often be handled via the standard electronic path. [3, 7, 9]

Transit Visa (Transit): For individuals traveling through Uzbekistan to a third country. It is valid for up to 3 days and requires proof of an onward ticket and a visa to your final destination. [10]

Pilgrimage/Ziyorat Visa: A dedicated tourist category issued to foreign citizens traveling specifically to explore religious, historical, and cultural heritage sites. [6]

Specialized & Long-Term Visas

These non-electronic visas are processed via an official invitation (Visa Support Letter) from an inviting entity in Uzbekistan and issued by an embassy or at Tashkent International Airport: [2, 11, 12]

Work Visa (E): Issued to foreign nationals legally employed by a registered company in Uzbekistan. This requires prior employment authorization from the Agency for External Labor Migration. [6, 7, 13]

chunks.title: Visa categories
chunks.content:
Work Visa (E): Issued to foreign nationals legally employed by a registered company in Uzbekistan. This requires prior employment authorization from the Agency for External Labor Migration. [6, 7, 13]

Student & Academic Visas (A-1 / Student): One-year renewable visas issued to students enrolled full-time in Uzbek educational institutions, or foreign researchers participating in academic exchanges. [6, 7, 14]

Vatandosh (Compatriot) Visa: A unique 2-year visa granted to individuals originally native to Uzbekistan and their family members, provided they are invited by relatives who are current Uzbek citizens. [14]

Investment Visa: A long-term multi-entry visa issued to foreign investors making significant financial or asset contributions to the local economy. Family members can be added under a dependent status. [15]

Medical Visa: Valid for up to 3 months for individuals entering the country for clinical treatment at an authorized medical facility, issued upon receipt of an official institutional invitation. [14]

chunks.title: Visa-free entry to Uzbekistan
chunks.content:
As of 2026, citizens from over 90 countries can enter Uzbekistan completely visa-free, with the permitted duration of stay ranging from 30 to 90 days depending on nationality. [1, 2]

The visual map below outlines global access, followed by the specific breakdowns by country and stay limits:

Up to 90 Days

Citizens of the following countries can stay in Uzbekistan for up to 90 days without a visa: [3]

Armenia

Azerbaijan

Belarus

Georgia

Kazakhstan

Moldova

Russia

Ukraine [4]

Up to 60 Days

Kyrgyzstan [4]

Up to 30 Days

Citizens of the United States, United Kingdom, European Union member states, GCC countries, and several others can enter visa-free for up to 30 days: [1, 5, 6]

Americas: United States, Canada, Argentina, Brazil, Chile.

Europe: All EU/Schengen countries (e.g., Germany, France, Italy, Spain), United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Monaco.

Asia & Oceania: Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Israel, Turkey, Mongolia, Tajikistan.

Middle East / GCC: United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain. [1, 5, 6, 7, 8]

Special Exemptions

Under 16: Foreign citizens of any nationality under the age of 16 enjoy visa-free entry for up to 90 days, provided they hold a valid international passport and travel with a legal guardian. [3, 9]

Uzbekistan permits visa-free entry for citizens of over 90 countries for periods ranging from 30 days to an unlimited stay. Eligible travelers simply present a valid passport at any border checkpoint without prior electronic or embassy applications.

Summary

Rule: Enter without a pre-arranged visa.

Duration: 30, 60, 90 days, or unlimited depending on nationality.

Key Duty: Mandatory local residence registration within 3 working days of arrival.

Overview

chunks.title: Visa-free entry to Uzbekistan
chunks.content:
Overview

Uzbekistan's simplified entry program promotes tourism and business. Eligible international travelers cross air, land, or rail borders seamlessly by bypassing consulate applications and fees.

Eligibility & Stays

Stays are categorized clearly by your passport origin:

Requirements & Documents

To pass through immigration smoothly, travelers must bring:

Valid Passport: Your national passport must be valid for at least 6 months past your arrival date.

Blank Pages: At least one empty page for entry and exit stamps.

Children's Papers: Minor travelers under 16 need their own biometric passport.

Proof of Transit: A valid ticket to a third country if utilizing the 5-day air transit exemption.

Application Steps & Processing

Steps: No advance application exists. Proceed straight to border control.

Time: Instant processing at the border counter.

Fees: $0 (Entirely free of consular charges).

Validity & Renewal

Validity: Clock starts the exact calendar day you clear border customs.

Renewal: Visa-free periods cannot be extended inside the country for tourist visits.

Visa Runs: Same-day exit and re-entry via a land border (a "visa run") resets the 30-day clock. No official cooling-off limit applies between visits.

Restrictions & Pitfalls

The 3-Day Registration Rule: You must register your location with immigration within 3 working days. Hotels handle this automatically and give you a physical slip. If staying with friends or in private rentals, your host must register you on the Emehmon portal.

Keep Slips: Keep all registration slips inside your passport. Border police might ask them when you exit the country.

Overstay Fines: Overstaying your visa-free window triggers fines and potential future travel bans.

Exceptions

chunks.title: Visa-free entry to Uzbekistan
chunks.content:
Exceptions

Under 16: Minors under 16 from any country enter visa-free for up to 90 days if traveling with a legally documented guardian.

Aged 55+: Seniors from Vietnam can visit visa-free for up to 30 days even if standard age groups from those countries require alternative tracks.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a return ticket to enter? Immigration rarely demands proof of onward travel at the gate, but keeping a flight copy handy prevents unexpected terminal delays.

What if my country is not on the visa-free list? You can instantly apply for a 30-day single or multi-entry tourist visa online via the Official Uzbekistan E-Visa Portal for a $20 fee.
